subject: Discovery call follow-up: rotating demo slots & next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery call follow-up: rotating demo slots & next steps

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery:
- Primary goals: reduce per-token inference cost, predictable latency for global users, and stronger audit / retention controls for regulated data.
- Key workloads: multi-tenant inference for customer-facing chat, embedding index updates, and occasional batch reranking.
- Constraints: EU data residency for a subset of traffic; APAC team wants a deeper look at quantization behavior on NVIDIA A10/RTX-class hardware.

Next step: 60-minute technical deep dive + live demo where we'll:
1) walk through a representative request path (prefix caching, batching),
2) show performance numbers on a similar workload, and
3) go over deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Because your team spans US / EU / APAC, I wanted to propose a rotating schedule so the same set of stakeholders can join without one region always taking nights. Proposed rotation (we rotate every week):

- Slot A (US-friendly): Tue 16:00 UTC, 9:00 PT / 18:00 CET / 01:00 JST
- Slot B (EU-friendly): Wed 08:00 UTC, 1:00 PT / 09:00 CET / 17:00 JST
- Slot C (APAC-friendly): Thu 23:00 UTC, 16:00 PT / 00:00 CET (next day) / 08:00 JST

Reality note: none of these are perfect for everyone. The rotation lets each region get one meeting in a reasonable local hour every three weeks and keeps total coordination overhead low. If you'd prefer, we can compress to two alternating slots (US/EU and EU/APAC), happy to adapt.

Can you confirm:
- which slot(s) work best for the extended team (including APAC contributors),
- whether week-on-week rotation is acceptable, and
- any hard blackout dates over the next 3 weeks.

I've attached the demo agenda and a short technical overview so your infra folks can skim prior to the call. Once you confirm preferred slots, I'll send calendar invites (ICS) adjusted to each participant's timezone.

Thanks, looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- demo-agenda.pdf (1 page)
- redwood-technical-overview.pdf (4 pages)

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 20:10:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Discovery call follow-up: rotating demo slots & next steps

Aditya,

Appreciate the clear recap. Kenji Sato (kenji.sato@zenko.jp) from our platform team will definitely join for the deep dive, he prefers APAC-friendly times. If we can avoid anything that lands after 02:00 JST that would be ideal.

My suggested approach: rotate between Slot A and Slot C so EU doesn't always get the late hour, but we avoid the very-early Wed/Thu windows.

If you can send a couple of concrete calendar options (or a Calendly/Doodle link) that maps to Kenji's timezone, I can confirm internally and lock in the invite.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Platform
Acme Corp

Samir,

Thanks, that makes sense. To keep things concrete, here's a two-week rotating pattern that avoids the very late-night slots while giving Kenji a reasonable local time on his meeting week:

- Week A (US-friendly): Tue 16:00 UTC, 9:00 PT / 18:00 CET / 01:00 JST (Kenji would join at ~01:00 JST)
- Week B (APAC-friendly): Thu 23:00 UTC, 16:00 PT / 00:00 CET (next day) / 08:00 JST (Kenji would join at 08:00 JST)

We can alternate A/B so Kenji only gets the late slot every other meeting. If you prefer we can shift Week A one hour earlier to bring Kenji to midnight instead of 01:00 JST; let me know which is better.

I've created tentative calendar invites and attached an ICS (redwood-demo-invite.ics), I'll only send final invites once you confirm the rotation and who from Acme will be on each occurrence. Also adding a HubSpot event for the deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACME-448.

Proposed next action: please confirm by EOD which pattern (A/B alternating) you'd like and the core participants for each meeting (especially any APAC folks besides Kenji). Once confirmed, Marissa will send final invites.

Best,
Aditya
